---
title: Tree routing and decoding
description: "Context moves from the leaves toward the root, and each decoder reads the context along its path."
engine: markdown
---

The model builds context from the leaves toward the root, then each requested
field decoder reads the context available along its schema path. The tutorial
has one `trxns` branch containing earlier payments and the latest payment.
Its fields build transaction context, and `disputed=rf.Boolean(mask=True)`
requests a dispute prediction at every retained transaction coordinate.

This explanation follows the
[execution plan](https://github.com/relflow/relflow/blob/8d9d6cfd8ce22a7819c2b5392c710d4f2cbe1a7c/src/relflow/architecture/runtime.py)
introduced in 0.2.4. The current pages are checked against RelFlow 0.3.6
([pinned source](https://github.com/relflow/relflow/tree/299413375f3c113e6750f75e81cb52736978b643)).

## Context moves toward the root

```{typst}
//| label: fig-mechanism-tree-routing
//| fig-alt: "An account snapshot has one repeated trxns branch containing earlier and latest payments. Each transaction has DateParts booked_at, Number amount, Category merchant, and Boolean disputed. Every dispute label is hidden and supervised for the same 30-day window after the common review cutoff."
//| fig-cap: "Connections show schema ownership. The transaction collection builds context, and the dispute decoder reads its path at every retained position."
#tree(node("account", kind: "root", body: [One decision snapshot.], children: (
  node("trxns", kind: "branch", repeated: true, body: [Earlier and latest payments.], children: (
    node("booked_at", type: "DateParts", body: [Selected calendar cycles.]),
    node("amount", type: "Number"),
    node("merchant", type: "Category"),
    node("disputed", kind: "target", type: "Boolean", body: [Hidden and supervised for every transaction.]),
  )),
)))
```

Each active leaf first supplies a field representation with its presence
information. The runtime sends it to its owning branch. Branches execute from
the deepest level upward, so a parent receives representations from its nested
branches after those branches have encoded and reduced their own children.

For this model, `trxns` processes the fields at its transaction positions first.
The root then receives the branch's output, without duplicate root amount or
merchant fields. With more nesting, the same rule repeats at each level.

Context also moves one step down before a branch encodes. Each branch reads
its parent's own fields at the record it belongs to: a learned projection of
their mean reaches every token in the branch, before its fields are mixed, and
its reduction queries. A transaction therefore knows the account it belongs to
before the history is summarized, and the summary can be collected with that
account in mind.
Branches at one depth form a group in the execution plan; this grouping
describes dependencies, without promising parallel execution.

The root is anonymous at `rf.Address()`. `account` in the figure describes the
observation; it does not add an address prefix. For schema construction and
addresses, see [Model tree](model-tree.qmd).

## A decoder reads its path

A target decoder receives the representations retained along its heritage:
the schema path through its ancestors to the field. Every ancestor branch
arrives twice: as the summary it sends to its parent and as its encoded
sequence, the tokens after that branch's own layers. A nested target can
therefore read individual sibling transactions and individual root fields as
well as their summaries. A branch with no decoded field beneath it only sends
its summary; its sequence is never materialized. Decoding starts after context
has been built; it does not reconstruct the input tree one parent prediction at
a time.

Query pooling uses learned queries shaped for the target's coordinates. Where
sibling representations align with those coordinates, the decoder can also
condition those queries on sibling context. The field's decoder then produces
the datatype-specific answer, such as the Boolean output for `disputed`.

The tutorial's `disputed=rf.Boolean(mask=True)` keeps every dispute label out
of the input and requests predictions at all retained positions. Training
supplies Boolean labels for all of them. Prediction can omit this directly
bound target from every transaction while retaining the input records that
establish those positions.

`embed=True` requests an exported contextual representation and adds no
reconstruction objective. These roles have their own explanations in
[Masking and reconstruction](masking-and-reconstruction.qmd) and
[Reusable representations](../learn/reusable-representations.qmd).

## Read the result

Output format 2 returns decoded fields in a `predictions` tree
and requested embeddings in a separate `representations` column. Only selected
columns appear. Repeated decoded siblings share one record collection; branch
representations retain their own output indices and ancestor coordinates.
[Read predictions](../learn/read-predictions.qmd) walks through one
payment's output and its state, content, and inference flag;
[Prediction output](../reference/prediction-output.qmd) is the full contract.

Continue with [Branch summaries](branch-summaries.qmd) for the information passed
between levels, or [How fields interact](how-fields-interact.qmd) for the context
built inside each branch.
